summary: INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION of f_optderive's work on src/opt/api.py and src/spine/derive.py. Every repro they cited was re-run against a FROZEN PRE-CHANGE TREE (git archive 40d2446^ -> scratch) and against the live tree, in fresh processes. ALL of their measurements reproduce EXACTLY -- flush_period(Steps(20000),16.9)=Flushes(1250), flush_period(Steps(20000),True)=Flushes(20000), nan->ValueError and inf->OverflowError out of int(), Decimal('16.5') and Fraction(33,2) both truncating to 16, run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(-1),10)=Windows(-10), opt_steps_from_windows(Windows(-1024),64)=Steps(1), FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=-500 -> FAB.d_manage_period=Flushes(1) and CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=-20000 -> FAB/TOK.d_cap_lift_period=Flushes(1) at build, RUN_EPOCHS -1/0/1 -> Windows(-634)/Windows(0)/Windows(634) -> Steps(1)/Steps(1)/Steps(634). Their ITEM 1 REFUTATION IS ITSELF CORRECT and I verified it independently against the frozen tree, not against their words: the false clause is nowhere in 40d2446^:src/opt/api.py and that file had no resume guard of any wording. THE CHANGES ARE NOT NARROWER THAN CLAIMED AND THEY REMOVE NOTHING ON THE ACCEPTED DOMAIN: a 792-cell direct-call differential over the six functions gives 144 changed cells, ALL of them a negative that used to answer becoming a UnitError, and ZERO non-negative answers moved; a 432-cell assemble.build lever sweep with only non-negative values gives ZERO differing cells; the same sweep with negatives gives 288 cells that went OK->UnitError and ZERO refusals lost. FIVE THINGS THEY DID NOT REPORT, three of them the shapes this round was told to hunt. (1) A FALSE EQUATION SURVIVES IN THE INVARIANT'S OWN ValueError, in the file f_optderive owns, ONE LINE BELOW the guard they added, and it is the SAME false equation and the SAME number (10) that the Gate three lines further down was repaired for on 2026-09-04: 'backward=16, accum=4, so 10 optimizer steps were due and 11 were taken' -- 16//4 is 4 -- and it is reachable at an UNCHANGED OPT_ACCUM too, on any resume whose boundary fell mid-accumulation ('backward=13, accum=4, so 2 optimizer steps were due and 4 were taken'; 13//4 is 3). (2) THE OWNER'S RULING ON THE PERIODS IS DEFEATED for FAB_MANAGE_EVERY: with src/fabric/api.py::REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD SET TO False the build still dies, because the new unswitched refusal in spine/derive.py fires at assemble.build before any Config exists -- measured. Turning the refusal off is now an edit to spine/derive.py, and fabric/api.py's own docstring sentence 'False lets the value through to units.Windows exactly as it did before 2026-09-04' is now FALSE. CAP_PIN_WINDOWS got the same unswitched hard refusal with no switch anywhere in the tree. f_optderive filed the REACHABILITY of this as unfinished; they did not file the RULING BREACH or the false docstring. (3) A DETECTION WAS REMOVED: tests/test_fabric.py::check_f8's OFF branch -- the clause that enforces D4's guarantee that OFF means exactly Windows(-5) -- is now DEAD CODE, proved by running F8 with the switch False on both trees (live: layer='the assembly', OFF never exercised; mutant with derive not refusing: layer='nobody', manage_period returned Windows(-5), the branch reached). (4) derive's refusal message NAMES THE WRONG LEVER on the CAP_PIN_WINDOWS coupling -- at CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=-5 the message's only concrete lever text is 'FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=-500 built FAB.d_manage_period=Flushes(1)' -- and that hardcoded prose is EXACTLY what makes F8's 'the refusal names the lever' assertion pass; I proved F8 is otherwise sensitive by planting a lever-less and a value-less message (both FAIL) and a correct one (PASS). (5) ALL NINE NEW GUARDS HAVE ZERO TEST COVERAGE, proved by mutation rather than asserted: with all six 'type(rate) is not int' tests and all four new negative-count tests replaced by 'if False:' (and int() coercion restored), the WHOLE SUITE IS GREEN -- derive 575 oracle cases 0 mismatches, smoke OK, fabric 8/8 including F8, contract 15+59, census 8, couplings 4. f_optderive filed this as unfinished[0] and the patch did not land. NOTHING I FOUND CONTRADICTS A NUMBER THEY PUBLISHED. Suite on the live tree, run by me: ownership 13+32 0 failing, contract 15+59 0, census 8 0, assemble 9 0, couplings 4 0, fabric 8 0, derive 575 oracle cases 0 mismatches. I edited no file; tests/_noise_floor.json was rewritten by the suite's own run and I restored it with git checkout, so `git status --porcelain` lists only untracked audit JSONs.

findings.detail: A FALSE EQUATION, IN THE FILE f_optderive OWNS, ONE LINE BELOW THE GUARD THEY ADDED, AND IT IS THE ONE THE GATE BESIDE IT WAS ALREADY REPAIRED FOR. src/opt/api.py:1533-1541 raises `f"OPT.counters: the accumulation invariant is broken -- backward={n_bwd}, accum={divisor}, so {due_steps + base_step} optimizer steps were due and {n_step} were taken."` -- n_bwd and n_step are the UNBASED run totals while due_steps is measured SINCE THE RESUME, so the sentence asserts n_bwd // divisor == due_steps + base_step, which is false whenever base_bwd is not an exact multiple of divisor. src/opt/api.py:1397-1403 and the comment at :1614-1626 describe this EXACT defect being repaired in the Gate on 2026-09-04 -- 'the line read "Gate opt.accum.invariant: FIRED (16 backward // 4 vs 10)". 16 // 4 is 4.' -- and the Gate at :1627 now correctly renders `f"{n_bwd - base_bwd} backward // {divisor}"` against int(taken). The ValueError three lines above it was not moved. I DROVE BOTH ARMS. Changed accum (their own documented resume): base=(8,8), accum=4, n_bwd=16, n_step=11 -> 'backward=16, accum=4, so 10 optimizer steps were due and 11 were taken'; 16//4 is 4 and 10 is the same number the Gate printed before its repair. UNCHANGED accum, which is the ordinary case and is why this is not a corner: a checkpoint saved mid-accumulation gives base=(10,2) at accum=4 (10//4 == 2, a perfectly sound parent), and n_bwd=13, n_step=4 -> 'backward=13, accum=4, so 2 optimizer steps were due and 4 were taken'; 13//4 is 3. The trailing `since` clause does print the two bases and the two deltas, so a careful reader can reconstruct the true statement -- but the headline sentence, in the one message whose stated job is proving ISSUES P3-H29 dead, states an equation its own printed numbers refute. This is the class the spine rules call worse than printing nothing, and three previous rounds put new instances of it in exactly this file. NOT INTRODUCED BY f_optderive -- it predates them -- but it is in their file, one line from their edit, and their own docstring paragraph :1397-1403 is about it.

findings.symbol: src/spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows -- the owner's ruling on the periods
findings.detail: THE REFUSAL IS NOT TURN-OFF-ABLE, WHICH IS THE HALF OF THE OWNER'S RULING D17 EXISTS TO KEEP. The ruling recorded verbatim at src/ckpt/api.py::REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD is 'On the periods, let's refuse for now. If it has a bad effect, we can turn off the refusal', and src/fabric/api.py::REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD states 'True is the shipped state; False lets the value through to units.Windows exactly as it did before 2026-09-04'. MEASURED ON THE LIVE TREE: with FAB.REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD set to False, assemble.build({'FAB_MANAGE_EVERY':'-5'}) STILL DIES -- 'UnitError: flush_period_windows: period_windows=Windows(-5) is negative' -- because the coupling compute at spine/assemble.py:787 runs inside build(), before any accessor and before any Config exists, and the new refusal at spine/derive.py:356 has NO SWITCH. So flipping the constant the owner asked for changes nothing for this lever, and turning the refusal off is now an edit to spine/derive.py. Two consequences neither f_optderive nor D17 recorded: (a) fabric/api.py's sentence about what False does is now FALSE for every value that reaches the assembly, which is every value from the environment; (b) CAP_PIN_WINDOWS was given the same unswitched hard refusal through the FAB.d_cap_lift_period and TOK.d_cap_lift_period rows, and CAP has no REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD at all -- so a sixth period lever acquired a refusal with no off switch anywhere in the tree, outside the five the ruling was asked about. CKPT_EVERY, DOM_MANAGE_EVERY, EVAL_EVERY and MEM_REKEY_EVERY are unaffected: none of them has a coupling row, so their switches still bind. f_optderive DID file the reachability of FAB's guard as unfinished[1] and explicitly concluded 'NOTHING NEEDS REMOVING -- D4 keeps a mechanism WITH a switch'; what they did not file is that the switch no longer switches anything on the path the environment takes, or that fabric/api.py now says something false about it. I am not asserting the refusal is wrong -- the ruling's first sentence orders it -- only that the second sentence no longer holds and nobody said so.

F8's docstring names the thing it exists to catch when the switch is off: 'the switch is off and OFF must mean exactly the pre-refusal behaviour, Windows(-5) -- and anything else is a third answer for one number', implemented as the `elif not isinstance(got, U.Windows) or int(got.n) != -5` clause and the `if layer == "FAB.manage_period" and not switch` clause. Both sit inside the `else:` of `try: c = cfg(FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=-5)`. On the live tree that `try` now RAISES, from spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows inside the coupling compute, so the `else:` is never entered and both clauses are unreachable through cfg(). MEASURED BOTH WAYS. Live tree, REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD forced False: F8 PASSES and its detail line reads 'at -5 the refusal came from the assembly (spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows, via the FAB.d_manage_period coupling) (REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD=False)' -- the OFF contract was never exercised. Mutant tree with derive's negative guards replaced by `if False:`, same switch False: F8 PASSES and reads 'at -5 the refusal came from nobody (REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD=False), and manage_period returned Windows(-5)' -- the branch is reached and the D4 contract is actually checked. F8 is not wrong to pass in either case: the property it names, 'a negative cadence never reaches a reader', genuinely holds. What is gone is the second property it also encodes, that OFF is a real configuration -- and F8's own detail line is the only place that says so, in prose, on a line nobody has to read.

findings.symbol: src/spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows -- the refusal message's lever name
findings.detail: THE MESSAGE NAMES A LEVER THAT DID NOT CAUSE THE FAILURE, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES F8's LEVER ASSERTION PASS. The refusal at spine/derive.py:356 hardcodes a narrative naming both couplings: 'FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=-500 built FAB.d_manage_period=Flushes(1), and CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=-20000 built FAB.d_cap_lift_period and TOK.d_cap_lift_period=Flushes(1)'. At CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=-5 the ONLY thing the message says about the failure itself is 'period_windows=Windows(-5)'; the two lever names and the two values it prints in full are both somebody else's, and the coupling that actually failed is never named. spine/assemble.py:1426 is a bare `value = c.compute(_view(c, configs))` with no try/except, so nothing upstream attaches the coupling either. THIS IS ALSO WHY tests/test_fabric.py::check_f8 GREENS ITS 'names the lever it read it from' ASSERTION: that assertion tests `any(sp in message for sp in ('FAB_MANAGE_EVERY','manage_every'))`, and it is satisfied by the narrative sentence, not by the message identifying the lever. I CONFIRMED F8 IS OTHERWISE SENSITIVE, both directions, by monkeypatching flush_period_windows inside the coupling: a message reading only 'flush_period_windows: period_windows=Windows(-5) is negative.' FAILS F8 ('names none of (FAB_MANAGE_EVERY, manage_every)'); a message naming the lever but not the value FAILS ('names none of (-5,)'); a patched function that ACCEPTS the negative PASSES, correctly, because FAB.manage_period then refuses it. So the check is real and the pass on the live tree is a string coincidence in one direction. Fixing it belongs in spine/assemble.py (wrap the compute and name the coupling) rather than in derive, which cannot know its caller.

findings.detail: THEIR REFUTATION IS CORRECT AND I ESTABLISHED IT FROM THE FROZEN TREE RATHER THAN FROM THEIR REPORT. `git archive 40d2446^ | tar -x` into scratch gives the tree as it stood before this round's commit. In it, `grep -rn 'missed every\|smaller than accum\|which missed\|flooring' old/src old/docs old/tests` returns exactly two hits, both pre-existing and both CORRECT sentences inside spine/derive.py's own opt_steps_from_backwards docstring (:669 'SIDE EFFECT of `//` flooring: floor(n/k) is at most -1 for every n < 0' and :673 'the same-day repair from flooring to TRUNCATION then'); nothing in opt/api.py. `grep -n 'went BACKWARDS\|n_backward) < base_bwd' old/src/opt/api.py` returns nothing -- the file had no resume guard in any wording. So the brief's premise that the false clause 'travelled before the correction and is still standing' in src/opt/api.py is false, exactly as they said. THE GUARD THEY LANDED INSTEAD IS SOUND AND ITS CITED FACTS ARE TRUE: opt/api.py:2192-2193 stamps opt.ckpt.backward_at_load/step_at_load AFTER the restore (I read the whole of load_state -- the two refusal branches return BEFORE restoring anything, so no refused load can leave a stale base), and opt/api.py:944 `st.n_backward = st.n_backward + U.Backwards(1)` is the only writer. THE GUARD REMOVES NOTHING AND MASKS NOTHING: its condition `int(st.n_backward) < base_bwd` is exactly the condition under which spine/derive.py::opt_steps_from_backwards would have raised one line later, so coverage is identical and only the message changes; and a step counter that fell without the backward counter falling is still caught, because `taken` is then negative while `due` is non-negative and `due != taken` cannot cancel. I drove it: base=(52,13) with n_bwd forced to 49 raises 'the backward counter went BACKWARDS across a resume -- backward=49 against opt.ckpt.backward_at_load=52, with step=13 against opt.ckpt.step_at_load=13'; base=(52,13) with n_bwd=56 n_step=12 falls through to the invariant, as it should. The clean case is unmoved: 52 backward passes at OPT_ACCUM=4 give opt_step=13 and Gate opt.accum.invariant FIRED with value '52 backward // 4' and threshold 13. ONE INACCURACY IN THE REPORT ITSELF, not in the code: they cite the stamping as 'opt/api.py:2158' and it is at 2192-2193; 2158 is inside the param_group_shape refusal branch.
